comment: HARDWARE PROBE, not a release effect. Answers: when the Patch Editor writes a patch (0x28) to a slot-4..6 effect, does ANY host-owned region the DSP can see change? Hashes a window behind each ctx[] pointer every block and blips that word's index when its hash moves (3 blips = ctx[3]). Skips the audio buffers ctx[4]/[5]/[6]/[12]/[13]/[14], which change every block by definition. ctx[1] (params table) is watched as the CONTROL -- on slots 4-6 it should NOT react, which is the whole bug. If some other word blips, a custom effect could read its knobs from there instead of params[] and behave the same on all six slots with no bypass bounce. DEREFERENCES ctx words behind a guard (non-zero, 4-aligned, inside the host arena window); a bad deref is exactly how this DSP hard-freezes, so back up patches first -- a freeze is cleared by rewriting from Effect Manager.
gid_comment: 0x07 = SFX category, matching the other probes; keeps diagnostics out of the Delay group with the release pack.
fxid_comment: 0x01BF. Free: no stock effect uses it and it is not a retired custom alias. Probe-only, never shipped in dist/.

params.name: Span
params.comment: How many 32-bit words to hash behind each pointer, 8..256. Wider catches more but is likelier to include something that churns on its own.
